claim: A member can end up holding more than four books at the same time, even though the limit is four.
why: The limit check runs only when a member asks to borrow, so borrowing a fifth book directly is refused. When a returned book goes to the next member in the queue, give_back adds it to that member's loans without any check. A member with three loans can queue for a taken book, borrow a fourth, and then receive the queued book as a fifth; the README's claim that every route is checked is false.

deciding.note: direct borrow of a fifth book is refused
queue hand-over in give_back adds a loan with no limit check

root.claim: A member can hold more than four books at once

atoms.claim: Borrowing a fifth book directly is accepted
atoms.evidence: borrow raises ValueError when len(held) >= LIMIT; test_library.py shows it.

atoms.claim: A returned book handed to a queued member can push that member past four loans
atoms.evidence: give_back adds to loans with no limit check; run: bob holds 3, queues x, borrows d, ann returns x, count is 5.
